ai.title: Track reused CLI auth tokens
ai.summary: CLI login token consumption now updates `verificationToken` to a consumed state instead of deleting it. This allows the system to distinguish between missing and already-used tokens, surfacing specific errors to the user. The change affects `freebuff/web` and `web` packages, specifically `_db.ts`, `_helpers.ts`, and `page.tsx`. Consumed tokens are marked with `cli-login-consumed:<token-hash>` and scrubbed of sensitive data.

eli5.text: If you sign in to the CLI and then try to use the same login token a second time, you will now see a clear error telling you the token was already used, instead of the system silently deleting it and treating it like it never existed. The system now keeps a record of used tokens, marked as consumed, so it can tell the difference between a token that was never valid and one that was already claimed. This affects anyone who logs in through the CLI and tries to reuse the same browser-based verification step.

ai.title: OpenCode Zen model registry and guard tightened
ai.summary: Removed opencode/minimax-m2.7 from openCodeZenModels and OPENCODE_ZEN_MODELS. isOpenCodeZenModel switched from prefix check to in-operator lookup against the registry. getOpenCodeZenModelId fallback now returns model unchanged. Covers common/src/constants/model-config.ts and web/src/llm-api/opencode-zen.ts.

eli5.text: The assistant can no longer start a conversation using the minimax-m2.7 model through the OpenCode Zen path; that option has been removed entirely. You select a model from a fixed list rather than by typing a name starting with "opencode/", so only kim k2.6 remains available there. If you tried to request minimax-m2.7, it now comes back unchanged instead of being translated to a different model id, meaning it won't work as before. This is live now.

ai.title: Allow more European countries in free mode
ai.summary: Added France (FR), Italy (IT), Spain (ES), and Portugal (PT) to FREE_MODE_ALLOWED_COUNTRIES in web/src/server/free-mode-country.ts. Updated the FAQ text in freebuff/web/src/app/home-client.tsx to reflect the new availability. This change expands the geographic scope for the free mode feature. The update is purely additive to the existing allowlist and documentation.

eli5.text: Freebuff is now available in France, Italy, Spain, and Portugal, in addition to the countries that already had access. If you visit the site from one of these four European countries, you will now be able to use the free mode without restrictions. The FAQ page has been updated to reflect the expanded list of supported countries.
